newsitem.title: FRANCE: DHL hits setback in plans for Strasbourg hub.
newsitem.headline: DHL hits setback in plans for Strasbourg hub.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express's plans to build a regional air cargo hub at Strasbourg city airport suffered a major setback on Tuesday when the Chamber of Commerce asked it to withdraw the controversial proposal "in its current form."
The Chamber of Commerce, which manages the airport, said in a statement it had been unable to conclude that the cargo hub would not bother city residents.
Gilles Garin, chairman of DHL France, said that the express distribution group still hoped to build the hub at Strasbourg.

"As long as they have not said clearly 'no', we are still interested," he told Reuters by telephone. "It is up to Alsace to see whether they want us. If not, we will go elsewhere. But Alsace is the best place for us."
Last weekend, some 12,000 people demonstrated against the proposed hub, saying that the flights would keep locals awake at night.
A report last week by three leading local officials including Mayor Catherine Trautmann said the plan was unacceptable.
DHL had planned one or two nightly flights from Strasbourg using Convair and Electra aircraft in late 1996, rising to seven a night next year.
Deutsche Lufthansa and Japan Airlines Co Ltd each hold a 25 percent stake in DHL.
